name: Smirgat

attributes.attribute: one of the wives of Fionn and a prophet
warned that drinking from a horn would kill Fionn
always drank from a goblet to escape the doom

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Smirgat is a heroine of Ireland. Her second name is Smirnat. She was one of the wives of Fionn mac Cumhaill, the great leader of the Fianna. Smirgat could see the future. She told Fionn of the doom that would fall if he drank from a horn. The hero took her warning to heart. From that day he drank only from a goblet. The prophecy of Smirgat stayed close at hand and moved him to change his habit. The story marks the seer as the one that guards the king, and the house of a faithful wife who spoke the true word. The horn and the goblet show the small choice that turns a death away.
